summary: Eday Airport (EOI) is a small island airstrip located on the Orkney island of Eday in northern Scotland, serving as a vital transport link for the remote island community. The airport primarily handles inter-island flights within the Orkney archipelago, with scheduled services connecting to Orkney's main airport at Kirkwall. Its single gravel runway accommodates small turboprop aircraft, making it one of the most northerly operational airfields in the British Isles.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate from Eday Airport?
A: Eday Airport is primarily served by Loganair, which operates scheduled inter-island flights within Orkney, typically connecting to Kirkwall Airport on the Orkney mainland.

Q: How long is the runway at Eday Airport?
A: The single runway at Eday is a relatively short gravel strip suitable for small turboprop aircraft such as the Britten-Norman Islander used on inter-island routes.

Q: Are there car rental services at Eday Airport?
A: No commercial car rental services operate at Eday Airport due to its small size. Most travellers arrange private transport or use local contacts on the island in advance.

Q: When is Eday Airport open for flights?
A: Flight schedules at Eday typically align with daylight hours and operate year-round, though timetables can be limited and weather-dependent due to the exposed northern location.
transport_tips: Eday is a small island with no public bus service, so arranging private transport in advance with a local contact or your accommodation provider is recommended. The journey from Kirkwall to Eday by ferry takes approximately 1.5 hours, offering an alternative to flying for travellers carrying heavy luggage or vehicles. Taxis are not generally available at the airport, so pre-booking essential transport before arrival is strongly advised.
local_tip: Bring cash in small denominations for any local purchases or tips, as mobile signal and card payment facilities can be unreliable on this remote island — locals appreciate when visitors are prepared for off-grid conditions.
